headline: Thirteen innings of insanity as the Red Sox streak reaches eight
morning_brew: I was about to throw my remote through the screen when Caleb Durbin finally lined that single to center and sent us all home happy in the thirteenth. It was a long, draining night at Fenway that took three years off my life, but winning eight straight is the kind of stuff that has the whole city vibrating. My neighbor Rick has been spending his week building a dossier on the challenge system, and even he had to shut his mouth and admit that watching us grind out a win like that is what the game is supposed to be.

Brayan Bello looked like a rock when the game was on the line, and watching our guys rally over and over against Chicago proved they aren't gonna fold when the pressure gets heavy. We had runners everywhere all night, and it felt like every time we needed a big knock to keep the season rolling, someone stepped up and answered the bell. It is the kind of performance that makes you forget about the shaky early innings and just enjoy the ride, because this team has finally figured out how to win the nail-biters.

We have the Athletics in town for a few more days before heading to Toronto, so we cannot afford to get comfortable now. Every single victory matters when we are fighting for ground in the East, and playing with this much heart is exactly how we keep climbing the ladder. I am feeling wicked good about this rotation and the way the bench is contributing, so let's see if we can make it nine tonight and add another healthy deposit to the Duck Boat fund.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox rally again and again, then beat White Sox in 13
news_digest.dans_take: Winning in extras is never pretty, but it counts just the same in the standings, and I'll take it.

news_digest.headline: Jaylen Brown says trade to Sixers has been 'crazy transition'
news_digest.dans_take: It is still a gut punch to see him in a different jersey after everything he gave to Boston.
